Package org.apache.juneau.rest.server.mcp.v20260728

Record Class McpMrtrResumeContext

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
org.apache.juneau.rest.server.mcp.v20260728.McpMrtrResumeContext
Record Components:
continuation - The decoded continuation, exactly as RequestStateCodec.unseal(java.lang.String, java.lang.String, java.security.Principal) produced it. Can be null if the handler paused with a null continuation. See the round-trip contract above: it is generic JSON, not the original Java type — use continuationAs(Class) to recover a typed view.
inputResponses - The client's collected answers, echoed from the follow-up request's inputResponses field. Never null (an empty map when the client sent none).
public record McpMrtrResumeContext(Object continuation, Map<String,Object> inputResponses) extends Record
Bean stashed into the BeanStore passed to a handler on a RESUME call, carrying the decoded continuation and the client's collected answers.

Absent (not stashed) on a first-round call — a handler that only ever completes in one round never has to know this type exists. A resumable handler calls ctx.getBean(McpMrtrResumeContext.class) to detect resume and retrieve both fields.

Per-round arguments are client-controlled; the continuation is not. On RESUME the handler receives its ordinary arguments from the follow-up request — the client re-sends them each round and full schema validation runs per round, but nothing about the original round's arguments is sealed or verified, so a client can alter them between rounds and the MRTR layer will accept the resume. Only continuation() (sealed by RequestStateCodec, AEAD-authenticated) is tamper-evident across rounds. Therefore any value a handler must trust across rounds must be carried in the continuation, never re-read from the per-round arguments. The client is expected to re-send the original arguments on every round; a handler that needs the exact original arguments should stash them in the continuation rather than rely on the client echoing them faithfully.

Continuation type fidelity (round-trip contract). continuation() is whatever RequestStateCodec.unseal(java.lang.String, java.lang.String, java.security.Principal) decoded from the client's echoed requestState: a generic JSON value (JsonMap/JsonList/boxed primitive/String), never the original Java type the handler threw in McpInputRequiredSignal (see the type-fidelity note on McpRequestState). Rather than force handler authors to parse that generic value by hand, continuationAs(Class) converts it back to any Juneau-marshallable target type in one call, so a handler that paused with a bean recovers a bean of the same shape ergonomically.

  • Method Details

    • continuationAs

      public <T> T continuationAs(Class<T> type)
      Returns the continuation converted to the given type.

      Convenience for the round-trip contract documented on this record: because continuation() is a generic JSON value (not the handler's original Java type), a handler that paused with, say, a ResumeState bean would otherwise have to reconstruct it manually from a JsonMap. This converts the generic value to type via Juneau's JSON marshaller — the same mechanism the codec used to serialize it — so continuationAs(ResumeState.class) returns a fully populated ResumeState.

      Failure contract: conversion is best-effort against a generic JSON value. If the continuation's decoded shape is incompatible with type, the underlying marshaller throws (a RuntimeException); a handler that lets it propagate surfaces the -32603 internal-error fail-safe from McpRevision#dispatch. A handler that pauses and resumes with a single, consistent continuation type never hits this.

      Type Parameters:
      T - The target type.
      Parameters:
      type - The target type to convert the continuation to. Must not be null.
      Returns:
      The continuation converted to type, or null if the continuation is null.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - If type is null.
      RuntimeException - If the continuation's decoded shape cannot be converted to type.

    • continuationAsString

      public String continuationAsString()
      Returns the continuation as a String.

      Convenience for the common case documented on continuationAs(Class): a handler that pauses with a plain String continuation can call this instead of spelling out continuationAs(String.class) at the headline pause/resume call site.

      Conversion is not lenient. continuationAs(String.class) routes through the JSON marshaller, which parses String the same as any other target type — it requires a quoted JSON string literal, so a continuation that decoded to anything else (a bare number, a JsonMap, a JsonList, a boolean) throws below rather than being stringified. Only a continuation whose decoded shape is already a String converts successfully.

      Returns:
      The continuation as a String, or null if the continuation is null.
      Throws:
      RuntimeException - If the continuation's decoded shape is not already a String.
